City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
November 19, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:05 p.m. , on November 19, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on November 14, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht
INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received personnel information, provided direction to staff and continued the matter to a future date. There was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance Corporal Darryl J. Armstrong, and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Evan A. O'Callaghan.
P2.
Never Ever Give Up (NEGU)/ Jessie Rees Foundation - Help support kids fighting cancer by donating items to fill Joy Jars
The City Council received the presentation from Mayor Pro Tem Reardon and the Spinello family.In an effort to support the Spinello family, the Jessie Rees Foundation and children battling cancer, the City of Mission Viejo will launch the NEGU JoyJars project at the Santa's Arrival celebration on Sunday, November 25. Subsequently, residents can donate specific JoyJar items in specially marked boxes at City Hall (200 Civic Center), the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center (24932 Veterans Way) and at the Mission Viejo Library (100 Civic Center) through December 14.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Gail Reavis, M.V.: congratulated Cathy Schlicht on her re-election and she asked the City Council Members to put campaign finance limits in place. She stated that without reform, Mission Viejo voters will continue to be bombarded and abused by special interests. Lastly, Mrs. Reavis noted that the City Attorney will be speaking about Kaleidoscope signage this evening and she lodged her complaint that the matter is not on the agenda.
Leticia Mata, OC Human Relations, Santa Ana: shared the OC Human Relations Annual Report and outlined the number of Mission Viejo families that were helped by their services. Ms. Mata thanked the City for supporting OC Human Relations and she presented Mayor Ury with a certificate of recognition.
Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: speaking as the City's Casta del Sol Homeowners Association liaison, she discounted Gail Reavis' comments on the Casta del Sol Golf Course. Mrs. Saltzgiver stated that residents succeeded in stopping the sale of the golf course in 2008 and they can do it again if necessary. Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: requested that the Council consider placing an item on the agenda to prohibit a Council Member from voting on a matter that affects the entity or corporation if it donated $250 or more to the Council Member.
Helen Workun, M.V.: on behalf of the Mission Viejo Heritage Committee, she reminded residents of two unique items: the Mission Viejo history book which is now available for $15.00 and a set of Mission Viejo playing cards for $5.00. Both are available at the library's reference desk and make great holiday gifts. Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: discussed the history of the NEGU organization and she stated that she is very pleased and proud that Mission Viejo gets involved in good things like the NEGU JoyJars project. Mrs. Bucknum announced that she was very privileged and pleased to run for City Council alongside Mayor Ury and she appreciated the support that she received from the community during the campaign.
Harry Lenczyk, M.V. (via email): asked the City Council to disapprove electronic billboards and external signs at the Kaleidoscope building and to maintain the Master Plan as discussed at the November 5 City Council Meeting.

Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as outlined below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

Mission Viejo Library Story Time Room Remodel (CIP 601) - Notice of Completion
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorize the payment of the final retention of $18,869.31, 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern that OCFA has not put broker-dealer work out for Board of Director annual approval and therefore, he contended, that the work was illegal because it was not authorized by the Board.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS
City Manager's Report
16.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the report and outlined staff's meeting with officials from the State Department of Finance earlier in the day.
City Attorney's Report
By consensus, the City Council members directed that the City Attorney's Report be presented in verbatim form for the Minutes:
City Attorney Curley : Thank you Mayor and Council. I have less a report in the sense of a formal, thorough report. I just wanted to pass some information along. I wanted to assure everybody that Ms. Reavis' concerns about Brown Act noticing are not correct. You are entirely safe and consistent in conformance with the Brown Act. The community has been aware and expressed concern over the advent or potential advent of electronic billboards as kind of a generic title to them. And they've been attached to the Kaleidoscope project as it has posed to the Council its interest in the last six months. I received, from the Kaleidoscope attorney, an incomplete, a foundational if you will, draft of the Development Agreement, about a week ago now. The reason I received it is it is not unusual because a Development Agreement is a contract, attorneys end up drafting them so they exchange back and forth between the attorneys. On the City side, certainly Mr. Wilberg, Chuck Wilson and his personnel, and any other necessary people will be looking at this proposal. And again, it is not an application; it is not something formally before the City. In essence, it's their version of what they think they would like to formally submit to the City at a future point. They're asking staff to give reaction to it. Staff will be doing that, in essence giving thought on what they proposed, recommended additions, deletions, whatever it may be. We haven't commenced that analysis so I can't tell you at all what it is. And the Brown Act requires something to be noticed if we're going to have an action on it or substantive discussion on the item. I don't want to talk about the Development Agreement because it is so barebones right now, there really is nothing to talk about. Again, I just wanted to let the Council know... and this was in consultation with Mayor Pro Tem Reardon during our agenda prep period. We thought it very important. She particularly wanted the community to know there is some stirrings of life. It is nothing ready - if you remember the old commercial, "No it's not soup yet," and just hitting the ground with this but didn't want anybody to not know that there is some stirrings of life so there was a thought just to let you know that it's revving up but nothing beyond that to tell you.
Mayor Ury : Alright, anything else?
City Attorney Curley : No sir.
Mayor Ury : All right. Now, we're going to Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon : Bill, would you please explain two things. Number one, what is the due process for the applicant? What does that mean? It's been thrown around... not so much tonight but in the past, for Kaleidoscope.
And then secondly, would you please explain the process that Kaleidoscope needs to be in, is in, should be in, will be in - in order to get whatever proposal they will end up having, to get to the Council for a vote. There's... we're a long way from there.
City Attorney Curley : Absolutely right. We're a long way. Your first question, again due process comes in two flavors if you will, two prongs. One is called procedural due process which means following the proper adopted adoption protocols - that will really be part of the second question you asked.
The first part of due process is a substantive due process, essentially meaning fairness. The decision makers in the City, the Planning Commission and the City Council, need to look at every proposal from every land owner with an open mind, make their decisions based on the facts and evidence before them. Certainly emotion has its place in all of that but you have to have the fixed, final proposal from that land owner before you. Preliminary proposals, rumors, suspicions, past proposals - none of those really apply and if those become the guidepost by which your decision makers act, then you have failed in due process, violated their right to a fair decision.
So that's why we are being very careful in not disclosing the preliminary terms and conditions, they are not to be disclosed, that's fairly clear in the law. Let the applicant get its - putting it basically - let them get their act together. Once they do, and we have a fixed rather than moving target, then everybody - public, staff, Council, surrounding Councils - everybody then has their opportunity to contribute their thoughts.
Going to the second part of your question, the substantive due process. Mission Viejo has adopted its own ordinances. They're based on State law, they are consistent with State law, but they are a little more rigorous. And the way it would work or does work here, the applicant, when they are ready, will file a formal submittal with Mr. Wilson, the Director of Planning, with all the fees and paperwork that's required. That is analyzed by staff and then it's presented to the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission does its review on it, its recommendations, whatever they may be, forwards those then to the City Council.
The City Council - and these are all at public hearings so everybody gets to comment. The City Council then has it at a public hearing, considers what's proposed and can either accept it, reject it or amend it. Conditions of approval, if you will. If it is your choice to go forward, you would tell staff - Mr. Wilberg and I and Mr. Wilson - "All right staff, put together a final contract, a final agreement with X, Y and Z terms in it" and "Staff, prepare the adoption ordinance."
You have to always keep in mind that while a development agreement is a land use entitlement and it is a contract, it is also a legislative action so you adopt it by ordinance. It is specifically referendable if the community is unhappy with it, a referendum could be brought to undo it or modify it. So, Planning Commission, City Council, City Council hearing, City Council direction to prepare the document, City Council consideration, separately then, thereafter, the adoption of that ordinance to adopt it.
Running parallel with that is the CEQA process - the environmental impacts of whatever the project is - are assessed. So there is a lot of sequential moving parts. All of them are tipped heavily toward public hearing and public input so it is by far probably the most publicly involved land use entitlement your Code has in it. And so at that point, after it's been through three or four or five hearings, everybody will hopefully have had their say, the Council will have a lot of wisdom to ponder and you'll give us direction. So if you think of each one of those hearings it will take a really long time.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon : Council Member Leckness is like, dying over there (inaudible.)
City Attorney Curley : Given the community concern, I didn't want anybody to misunderstand the process.
Mayor Ury : No that's fair, that's fair. Council Member Schlicht.
Council Member Schlicht : Thank you, then a request that I would have that this segment of the Attorney comments be recorded as verbatim minutes. Can I have Council consensus on that?
Mayor Ury : Sure, fine.
Council Member Schlicht : Okay. Thank you.
Mayor Ury : Council Member Leckness.
Council Member Leckness : Mr. City Attorney, isn't it true - no, no. (Laughter.) No, to answer or no, to ask... you use the phrase "Is it soup yet?" Which, I like that, because that's a great phrase, first of all. Lipton Soup it was. But how long will we be asking that question? Both Mayor Pro Tem Reardon and you use the term "long term." So does that mean we will be discussing this as a Council perhaps in December or are we talking June or somewhere in between? I mean what does a long ways mean?
City Attorney Curley : Well, I'll give you an elusive answer to that, hopefully not a long one. It will all be triggered by when the applicant formally submits the application. When they submit it, Chuck will put it on the first available Planning Commission after they've analyzed it. Thereafter it will come to the first available Council Meeting. Thereafter the ordinance would come to the first available Council Meeting. So the actual process will probably be about three months, consider. The predicate, getting ready to it, depending on their CEQA document, depending on what they decide they want to put in or not put in... that's all in their control. So if they come in tomorrow, three or four months. If they come in in six months, you know eight to ten months.
Council Member Leckness : Thank you.
Mayor Ury : All right. Super. Anything else?
City Attorney Curley : That's the full soup.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
17.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Community of Character Evening of Thankfulness and she commended the committee's youth for planning and executing a wonderful event. She also attended the City's Veterans Day ceremony which, she noted, gets better every year. She thanked staff and she publicly congratulated the two veterans of the Year, Bruce Hunt and Valorie Lephart. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the grand re-opening of Conroy's Flowers and she encouraged residents to visit the store. She also reminded residents that Santa will come to Mission Viejo on Sunday, November 25, 2012. There will be booths and activities from 3:00 to 5:00, entertainment from 5:00 to 6:00, at which time Santa will arrive at the Civic Center atop a fire truck. She also invited residents to visit Santa in his workshop every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from November 28 through December 19, from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character quality for the month of November is thankfulness and she read a quote from Calvin Coolidge's Thanksgiving Proclamation: "We have been a most favored people. We ought to be a most grateful people. We have been a most blessed people. We ought to be a most thankful people." Council Member Kelley concluded her comments by wishing residents a happy Thanksgiving holiday.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness discussed his attendance at the recent Chamber of Commerce Mixer which was held at the Mission Viejo Country Club. He reminded residents that they can become a social member of the Country Club for only $125 a month. Social members have unlimited use of the facilities and golf course privileges one time per quarter. Council Member Leckness thanked Brad Shupe, General Manager of the Country Club, and he encouraged residents to take advantage of the great offer.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht announced that she too attended the Chamber of Commerce Mixer and she is proud to declare that in a year's time, Chamber membership is up to about 200. She thanked the community for helping her to win her re-election and she noted that it has been a privilege to be on the City Council. She stated that she was up against a lot of special interests money and true to form, grassroots efforts always win. Council Member Schlicht thanked the Diablo football organization for a great season and she stated that they did the community proud. She also outlined her attendance at the City's Veterans Day recognition ceremony and the American Legion's pancake breakfast. She encouraged residents to get involved with American Legion and she stated that she hopes the organization can be involved, once again, with the City's ceremonies celebrating veterans. Council Member Schlicht encouraged residents to attend the Metrolink Toy Express on December 15 at 5:45 p.m. and to bring a toy for the Spark of Love toy drive. She wished everyone a happy Thanksgiving and ended her comments with a quote from Dwight D. Eisenhower: "A people that values its privileges above its principles soon loses both."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon congratulated Council Member Schlicht and Mayor Ury on their re-election to the City Council and she thanked them both for all that they do for the City. She stated that diversity of opinion is very beneficial and she commended them for keeping politics off the dais during their campaigns. She also outlined her attendance at the recent Nadadores diving exhibition and the Community of Character event, agreeing with Council Member Kelley that there are some wonderful young people on that Committee. She recounted her attendance at the Veterans Day ceremony and her conversation with a resident who attended the event for the first time. The resident told her that he was overwhelmed and it made him proud to be a resident of Mission Viejo. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon also attended the very informative Orange County Aging Services Alzheimer's event at the Mission Viejo Country Club and she reminded residents that NEGU will have a booth at Santa's Arrival event to kick off the project for collecting items for JoyJars. In light of Thanksgiving, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon shared a quote from William Bradford: ""All great and honorable actions are accompanied with great difficulties, and both must be enterprised and overcome with answerable courage." She noted that there were great examples of courage earlier in the meeting when the Marines were recognized, along with Cade Spinello and his family. Cade is a warrior and he is an example of courage and gratitude every day. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon concluded her comments by wishing everyone a blessed Thanksgiving and she expressed that she is grateful to be a member of the City Council.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury stated that the Veterans Day ceremony was a wonderful event and it is clear that Mission Viejo values and loves its veterans and service men and women. He also outlined his attendance at a recent Association of California Cities-Orange County meeting for newly elected Council Members. He noted that there are good people coming into office in Orange County who have the energy to help with the work of fixing the State. Mayor Ury announced that the City Council will be voting on a dog park at the December 3 meeting and he wished everyone a happy Thanksgiving.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 7:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, December 3, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
